# nself update

<!-- BEGIN PROSE:summary -->
> Update the ɳSelf CLI binary and admin UI.
<!-- END PROSE:summary -->

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED:synopsis -->
<!-- GENERATED BY tools/wikigen — DO NOT HAND EDIT -->

## Description

<!-- BEGIN PROSE:description -->
`nself update` checks for new releases of the ɳSelf CLI on GitHub (`nself-org/cli`) and installs the latest version. It replaces the current binary in-place and optionally restarts running services after the update.

By default, `nself update` updates both the CLI binary and the admin Docker image. Use `--cli` or `--admin` to update only one component. Use `--check` to see if an update is available without installing anything.

If you are running an active ɳSelf project and update the CLI, you may want to run `nself build --force && nself restart` afterward to regenerate `docker-compose.yml` with any new defaults from the updated version.

## Reviewing and applying pin changes (`--plan`, `--yes`)

A project's `nself.lock.yaml` pins the CLI minor, the CLI-owned images and the installed plugins. A CLI upgrade never moves those pins by itself, so an existing project moves to a newer Valkey, auth or Hasura image only when you ask:

```bash
nself update --plan          # print the old -> new pin table and the step list; writes nothing
nself update --plan --json   # the same as a v1 envelope (data.applied is false)
nself update --yes           # apply it
```

`--plan` compares the lock with the CLI image lock (images), the plugin registry (plugins) and the latest CLI release (cli). A pin the source no longer offers (for example a plugin deleted from the registry, or a release that answers 404) is a row marked `unresolvable` with the reason; it is never applied. If a source cannot be reached, or answers 429, the command fails with `E400` and prints no plan: an unreachable source is not an empty plan. The plugin registry is read strictly for planning: from its primary URL only, never from a stale cache. A plugin is resolved to the same free or licensed entry `plugin update` would install, and an image pin to the same variant (for example the pgvector build of postgres stays on pgvector). `--version vX.Y.Z` plans against that release instead of the latest. The plugin registry answer is cached in `~/.nself/cache/plugins`; that cache is the only thing `--plan` writes, and it is outside the project.

`--yes` runs, in this order: move the image pins in `nself.lock.yaml`, `plugin update` for each changed plugin, `nself build` (which rewrites the lock), then the CLI self-update last. `--cli=false` skips the CLI; `--cli` alone applies only the CLI. `--plan` and `--yes` cannot be combined, and `--json` needs one of them.

The step list is shared with `nself update stack`: backup, images, plugins, build, start, migrate, readiness, health, cli. `--yes` runs only the project-file steps and the CLI; the steps that need a running stack (backup, start, migrate, readiness, health) are reported as skipped and belong to `update stack`.

Moving an existing project to Valkey, the renamed `nhost/auth` image or the newer Hasura: run `nself update --plan`, read the image rows (`redis`, `auth`, `hasura`), then `nself update --yes`. The Valkey move recreates the cache container and does not migrate queued jobs; the auth and Hasura catalog migrations are one-way, so take a backup first (`nself backup create`) and, to roll back, restore it before pinning back.

## v0.9 legacy detection

When running on a v0.9 CLI (any `0.x.y` binary), `nself update --check` queries `ping.nself.org/version`, receives a migration block in the response, and surfaces the migration guide URL directly in the terminal:

```
WARNING: You are running a legacy v0.9 CLI. Migration to v1.1.1 is required.
Upgrade guide: https://nself.org/docs/migrate/from-v0.9
```

The check is read-only and non-destructive. It does not install anything. See [[Upgrade-From-v0.9]] for the full migration guide.
<!-- END PROSE:description -->

## Examples

<!-- BEGIN PROSE:examples -->
```bash
# Check for updates without installing
nself update --check

# Update CLI and admin UI to latest
nself update

# Update only the CLI binary
nself update --cli

# Update only the admin UI
nself update --admin

# Force update even if already up to date
nself update --force

# Install a specific version
nself update --version v1.0.0

# Update and restart services
nself update --restart

# Show the pin changes for this project, then apply them
nself update --plan
nself update --yes

# Apply the pins but leave the CLI binary alone
nself update --yes --cli=false
```
<!-- END PROSE:examples -->
